domains.NBT: Number and Operations in Base Ten

essentialElements.text: Starting with one, count to 10 by ones.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand number structures.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.CC.1. Starting with one, count to 10 by ones.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can starting with one, count to 10 by ones. I can Count number to 10 verbally.
I can count without one-to-one correspondence to 10 starting with one by rote.
I can sequentially sing numbers to 10 starting with one.

EE Approaching:
I can starting with one, count by ones to five. I can Count own fingers to five verbally.
I can sequentially, count sequence to five either independent of objects, pictures, or things as a student would recite the alphabet or by pointing. I can Count without one-to-one correspondence to five.
I can sequentially sing numbers to five. I can Sing along to counting song.

EE Emerging:
I can count with teacher from one to two. 
I can count with the teacher to two.

essentialElements.text: Connect counting to cardinality to 10.

subs.text: Demonstrate one-to-one correspondence, pairing each object with one and only one number and each number with one and only one object (one-to-one correspondence).
Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted (cardinality).

essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand number structures.

workbook.standard:
M.EE.K.CC.4. Connect counting to cardinality to 10.
 a. Demonstrate one-to-one correspondence, pairing each object with one and only one number and each number with one and only one object (one-to-one correspondence).
 Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted (cardinality).
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can starting with one, count to 10 by ones. I can count number to 10 verbally.
I can count without one-to-one correspondence to 10 starting with one by rote.
I can sequentially using numbers to 10 starting with one.

EE Approaching:
I can starting with one, count by ones to five. I can Count own fingers to five verbally.
I can sequentially, count sequence to five either independent of objects, pictures, or things as a student would recite the alphabet or by pointing. I can count without one-to-one correspondence to five.
I can sequentially using numbers to five. I can sing along to counting song.

EE Emerging:
I can count with teacher from one to two. 
I can count with the teacher to two.

essentialElements.text: Count out up to three objects from a larger set, pairing each object with one and only one number name to tell how many.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand number structures.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.CC.6. Count out up to three objects from a larger set, pairing each object with one and only one number name to tell how many.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can count out up to three objects from a larger set, pairing each object with one and only one number name to tell how many.
For example, I can take three blocks from a pile and count them one by one, saying "one, two, three." I know that there are three blocks in total.

EE Approaching:
I can count out up to three objects from a larger set, but I sometimes forget to say the number name for each object.
For example, I can take three crayons from a box and count them, but I might only say "one, two" instead of "one, two, three." I am still learning to connect each object with a number name.

EE Emerging:
I can start to count objects from a larger set, but I am still learning how to keep track of which objects I have counted.
For example, I can take some marbles from a bag and try to count them, but I might lose track and count the same marble twice. I am still developing my understanding of one-to-one correspondence.

essentialElements.text: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than (more) or less than (when the quantities are clearly different) or equal to the number objects in another group.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Compare, compose, and decompose numbers and sets.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.CC.7. Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than (more) or less than (when the quantities are clearly different) or equal to the number objects in another group.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can look at two groups of objects and tell you which group has more, less, or the same number of objects.
I can use words like "more," "less," and "equal" to describe the number of objects in different groups.
I can compare the number of objects in two groups by counting the objects in each group and comparing the numbers.
I can use objects to represent the numbers in two groups and compare the quantities.

EE Approaching:
I can sometimes identify which group has more or less objects, especially when the difference is large.
I can use the words "more" and "less" to describe the number of objects in different groups.
I can start to compare the number of objects in two groups by counting the objects in each group.
I can use objects to represent the numbers in two groups, but I may need help comparing the quantities.

EE Emerging:
I am starting to understand the concepts of "more" and "less."
I can sometimes identify which group has more objects when the difference is very obvious.
I am beginning to use objects to represent numbers.
I need support to compare the number of objects in two groups.

essentialElements.text: Represent addition as “putting together” or subtraction as “taking from” in everyday activities (e.g., with objects, fingers, sounds, drawings, verbal explanations, or numbers).
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Use operations and models to solve problems.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.OA.1. Represent addition as “putting together” or subtraction as “taking from” in everyday activities (e.g., with objects, fingers, sounds, drawings, verbal explanations, or numbers).
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can represent addition as “putting together” or subtraction as “taking from” in everyday activities.
I can identify the total number of crayons when one student has three crayons and another student has two, and they put their crayons together to share. Describe the action as put together.
I can add to a group of crayons when told to add to group.
I can take away from a group of crayons when told to take away from the group.
I can given five stickers, give another student one of the five stickers, and describes the action as take away.
I can join linking cubes to show action/process of putting together or addition.
I can break apart linking cubes/snap blocks/bristle blocks/pop-beads to show action/process of taking from or subtraction.

EE Approaching:
I can follow directions to “put together” by adding one or “take from” by taking one.
I can, if given a bowl of counting bears, add a counting bear to the bowl. The teacher calls the action “putting together” or addition.
I can take one when the teacher is passing out supplies and directs the students to take one. The teacher calls the action “taking away” or subtraction.
I can place popsicle sticks into a circle and use language to describe addition or “putting together”.
I can, using cubes, create towers by adding or taking away one cube at a time.
I can remove popsicle sticks from a circle and use language to describe subtraction or “taking from”.

EE Emerging:
I can put together” or “take from” with teacher.
I can together with a teacher add a block to a stack while teacher says, “put together.”
I can together with a teacher take a block from a stack while the teacher says, “take away.”

essentialElements.text: Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use geometric properties of two- and three- dimensional shapes.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.MD.1. Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can classify objects according to attributes (big/small, heavy/light).
I can, if given a big book and a small book, describe or demonstrate which one is bigger and which one is smaller.
I can, if given the shoe of a student and the teacher, identify which one is bigger and which one is smaller.
I can, sort heavy and light objects according to weight.
I can, if given the hand of a student in the class and the hand of the teacher, identify which one is bigger and which one is smaller.
I can, if given two objects of varying weight, describe or demonstrate which is heavy/light or large/small.

EE Approaching:
I can use a model or a template, sort objects by one attribute (big/small or heavy/light).
I can sort counting bears by size using a model or template.
I can, if given two objects, where one is at least twice the size of the other, identify which one is bigger and which one is smaller with descriptive prompts from the teacher.
I can identify bigger ball when shown a beach ball and a tennis ball, and listening to the teacher use voice inflections and kinesthetic motions to exaggerate bigger and smaller.
I can identify the bigger ball when shown a golf ball and beach ball and listening to the teacher using voice inflections and motions to exaggerate. I can Sort objects in the classroom into groups of heavy and light (e.g., bowling ball, beach ball, and a rock).
I can, if given two pictures of real-life objects, select the bigger one.

EE Emerging:
I can match objects by attribute big and small.
I can touch a large object (such as a pumpkin) as teacher describes it as big when compared to a smaller pumpkin toy.
I can indicate small pumpkin as teacher describes it as small when compared with a large pumpkin.
I can indicate if I want the big ball or the small ball.

essentialElements.text: Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use geometric properties of two- and three- dimensional shapes.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.MD.2. Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).

essentialElements.text: Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use geometric properties of two- and three- dimensional shapes.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.MD.3. Classify objects according to attributes (e.g., big/small, heavy/light).

essentialElements.text: Match shapes of the same size and orientation, including circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use geometric properties of two- and three- dimensional shapes.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.G.2. Match shapes of the same size and orientation, including circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can match circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles of the same size and orientation, even when they are presented in different arrangements or contexts.
I can identify and match shapes that are partially hidden or obscured.
I can explain how I know two shapes are the same size and orientation.

EE Approaching:
I can sort circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles into separate groups.
I can match two identical shapes, regardless of their orientation, from a small set of options.

EE Emerging:
I can identify circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles when they are pointed out to me.
I can match two identical circles when they are placed side-by-side.

essentialElements.text: Match shapes of the same size and orientation, including circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use geometric properties of two- and three- dimensional shapes.

workbook.standard: M.EE.K.G.3. Identify shapes as two dimensional or three dimensional
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target:
I can identify all basic 2D shapes, including circles, squares, triangles, rectangles, and ovals.
I can identify all basic 3D shapes, including spheres, cubes, cones, cylinders, and pyramids.
I can explain the difference between 2D and 3D shapes using my own words.
I can sort and classify shapes based on their dimensions.

EE Approaching:
I can identify some 2D shapes, like circles and squares, but I have trouble with other shapes like triangles and rectangles.
I can identify some 3D shapes, like spheres and cubes, but I have trouble with other shapes like cones and cylinders.
I can tell the difference between some 2D and 3D shapes, but I can't always explain why.

EE Emerging:
I can point to a shape and say its name, but I don't know if it is flat or solid.
I can sort shapes by color or size, but I don't understand the difference between 2D and 3D shapes.

essentialElements.text: Represent addition and subtraction e.g., by using objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), or acting out situations.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Use operations and models to solve problems.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.OA.1 Represent addition and subtraction e.g., by using objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), or acting out situations.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can use language to describe putting together and taking apart, aspects of addition and subtraction.
I can after the teacher shows six blocks and removes two, label the action as “take away” or informal language with the same meaning.
I can appropriately use “more” and “give” to express desire for more snacks or blocks.
I can use one-to-one correspondence to line up two sets of objects and ask which group has more/less.
I can during the practice of adding more to a numeral, show correct flashcard when asked, “I have two; who has two more (four)?”

EE Approaching:
I can put together or take away. I can Take away one crayon from the box.
I can put together red blocks and green blocks when asked.
I can give coins to purchase an item or take change at end of purchase. I can Give the teacher two blocks and then two more blocks.

EE Emerging:
I can follow directions to put together or take away an object with a verbal prompt.
I can In a classroom routine and when presented with a component needed for the routine, give component(s) when asked to put together for the activity.
I can take a paper or object from peer when passed out.
I can offer paper or object to peer to put together with group’s work when collected at the end of the lesson.

essentialElements.text: Use “putting together” to solve problems with two sets.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Use operations and models to solve problems.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.OA.2 Use “putting together” to solve problems with two sets.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can use “putting together” to solve problems with two sets.
I can Take attendance for a group of five or fewer students. Determine number of boys and number of girls. Put together number of boys and girls to determine how many classmates total.
I can Using name cards, determine for a group of five or fewer students the number of children who want to buy lunch from the cafeteria, and the number of children who brought a sack lunch. Put together the number of students eating lunch.
I can Line up for special class on numbers on classroom floor and tell how many students are in line.
I can Use counting sticks to solve a problem.

EE Approaching:
I can use “putting together” to solve a problem with one set and adding one more.
I can when given a set of counting bears (fewer than five), put together one more to make the next number.
I can When cleaning up the activity center, “put together” the toys, to make the next number (e.g., “I have two blocks. Can you put them together
with one more to make three?”).
I can Use dry erase board to solve a problem by adding one more.

EE Emerging:
I can put in an item from a group, using technology or objects. I can Drop one more bean bag into a bucket with a verbal prompt.
I can Drop one ping-pong ball into a Pringles can with hole cut into lid. I can Follow directions to add one counting block to a group.

essentialElements.text: Relate counting to addition and subtraction.

subs.text: Use manipulatives or visual representations to indicate the number that results when adding one more.
Apply knowledge of “one less” to subtract one from a number.

essentialElements.conceptualArea: Use operations and models to solve problems.

workbook.standard:
M.EE.1.OA.5.a Relate counting to addition and subtraction.
 a. Use manipulatives or visual representations to indicate the number that results when adding one more.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can use manipulatives or visual representations to indicate the number that results when adding one more.
I can there are four crackers on the table. “If I add one more, how many will I have?” The answer is five.
I can if three children are sitting at the table with four chairs, indicate “four” when asked, “How many will we have when Linda arrives?”
I can use tokens as positive reinforcement, the teacher points out that the student has five tokens, then adds one more and asks how many.

EE Approaching:
I can indicate the numbers that result when adding one more to the numbers from one to five.
I can add one more to a set of four objects.
I can when presented with four beads on a string, add one more.
I can while following the steps to play a game, add one more card to a set of cards.

EE Emerging:
I can do or give one more.
I can when asked, hand or give the teacher one more block. I can When asked, clap one more time.
I can use a Big Mac switch to request one more song, turn, or item with a teacher prompt.
I can in adaptive P.E., perform one more exercise, ball throw, etc. upon request.
I can look at a block when asked to give one more.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.OA.5.b Apply knowledge of “one less” to subtract one from a number.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can apply knowledge of “one less” to subtract one from the numbers.
I can Identify the number remaining when one object is taken away from a group of six objects arranged on the table.
I can when given five tasks to complete, tell how many tasks are left to complete before lunch as the teacher checks each off the list.
I can tell how many chairs are left each time when playing musical chairs as the teacher takes away one chair each time.
I can use a computer with touch screen and math software to click and drag objects one at a time away from total, determine how many are left each time an object is dragged away from the total set.

EE Approaching:
I can indicate how many are left when one is taken away from two to four objects.
I can with four counting cubes, take away one to leave three counting cubes.
I can when presented with four beads on a string, take away one and indicate how many are left.
I can when given four quarters, spend one at the school store and then tell the teacher how many quarters are left in bank.
I can use materials presented at a table, each student takes one as the group counts backwards.

EE Emerging:
I can remove or take one away.
I can erase one mark from a group of two on a dry-erase board. I can Take away one counting bear from a group of three.
I can take one block from a group of two.

essentialElements.text: Recognize two groups that have the same or equal quantity.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Use operations and models to solve problems.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.OA.7 Recognize two groups that have the same or equal quantity.

essentialElements.domainName: Number and Operations in Base Ten
essentialElements.text: Know the count sequence and understand numbers and quantities.

subs.text: Count up to 10 objects and represent the quantity with the corresponding numeral.

essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand number structures

workbook.standard:
M.EE.1.NBT.1a Know the count sequence and understand numbers and quantities.
 a. Count by ones to 30.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can count by ones.
I can participate in a classroom chant to count numbers 1 – 20. I can Recite the count sequence 1 – 20.
I can sing numbers to 20.

EE Approaching:
I can participate in a classroom chant 1 -10. I can Recite numbers 1-10.
I can sing numbers 1-10.

EE Emerging:
I can count to two.
I can sing numbers up to two with teacher.
I can count along using a voice output communicative device that will count in order (1-2) upon each activation.
I can activate a pre-programmed sequenced communication device repeatedly to recite the numbers one and two.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.NBT.1b  b. Count up to 10 objects and represent the quantity with the corresponding numeral.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can count as many as 10 objects and represent the quantity with the corresponding numeral.
I can Teacher will show the student numeral nine and ask them to give them that many blocks.
I can When shown the number five, count five crayons. I can Match a numeral card to a group of objects.
I can Write or draw the numeral that corresponds with the number of counting sticks.

EE Approaching:
I can count as many as five objects and/or represent the quantity with the appropriate numeral.
I can tap objects while counting.
I can during teacher-led counting/clapping routine, clap once for each number the teacher recites.

EE Emerging:
I can count up to two objects.
I can use tapping, switching, blinking, clapping, chanting to count two objects.
I can Hand items to peer one at a time, while peer counts.
I can Use eye gaze with large number line to look at each number as teacher counts.

essentialElements.domainName: Number and Operations in Base Ten
essentialElements.text: Create sets of 10.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Compare, compose, and decompose numbers and sets.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.NBT.2.a Create sets of 10.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can create sets of 10.
I can when given 20 crayons, divide them into two sets of 10.
I can when given 30 playing cards, pass out 10 cards to three players.
I can During calendar, students count out 10 straws to represent 10 days in school and bundles them and moves the bundle to the tens place pocket. I can Five students work cooperatively to count out 10 pennies each, combine and roll for the bank.

EE Approaching:
EE1.NBT.2. Create one set of 10 to match another set of 10.
I can Create one set of 10 using a model, or template to match another set of 10.
I can when given a set of 10 objects arranged in a row, make another row of 10 objects.
I can when given a hula hoop, group a set of 10 beanbags in it.
I can Count out enough toy rings for each of 10 fingers and put them on and check for accuracy.
I can Make a “bean stick” by counting out 10 beans and gluing them on a popsicle stick to match a model.
I can Access a switch that says “stop” or “that’s it” when watching or listening to another individual arrange sets or groups of 10.

EE Emerging:
EE1.NBT.2. Identify a set of five.
I can Select a set of five objects from a choice of two or more sets.
I can Choose from a set of markers and a set of crayons. (Exposure to vocabulary: set)
I can Choose from two sets of pictures the one that matches the model set of five.

workbook.standard: Not Applicable
Not Applicable

essentialElements.domainName: Number and Operations in Base Ten
essentialElements.text: Compare two groups of 10 or fewer items when the number of items in each group is similar.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Compare, compose, and decompose numbers and sets.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.NBT.3 Compare two groups of 10 or fewer items when the number of items in each group is similar.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can compare two groups of 10 or fewer items when the quantity of items in each group is similar.
I can when given two pencil boxes, one with five and one with 10 pencils, identify which pencil box contains the smaller set of items.
I can when given one set of cubes with 1-4 cubes, and a second set of cubes with 6-10, identify the set with less than five.

EE Approaching:
I can choose the matching set of items.
I can when given three pencil boxes, identify which two pencil boxes contain the same number of items.
I can when given three bracelets, match a second set of three bracelets from two choices.
I can when given one set of counting cubes with 1-4 cubes, and a second set of counting cubes with 6-9 cubes, identify the larger set.

EE Emerging:
I can match sets of one, two, or three objects .showing the same number of objects.
I can when given three sets of objects of one or two objects, match the two showing the same number.

essentialElements.domainName: Number and Operations in Base Ten
essentialElements.text: Compose quantities less than or equal to five in more than one way.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Compare, compose, and decompose numbers and sets.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.NBT.4 Compose quantities less than or equal to five in more than one way.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can compose numbers less than or equal to five in more than one way.
I can when given a set of red counting cubes and a set of green counting cubes, create a set of only red, a set of only green, and a set of mixed red and green totalling five in each case.
I can when given a five-piece inset puzzle and two trays, take out and sort the puzzle pieces into the trays in more than one way.
I can place colored macaroni pieces on each number on a number line up to five in any combination, then string.
I can shake two sizes of markers or painted beans in a cup and spill. Ask students to count each color and then count altogether.
I can draw circles and squares to make five in any combination.
I can use a muffin pan with five wells to place one colored block in each well, and then count to find the total.

EE Approaching:
I can identify (subitize) sets of one to three objects.
I can when given a set of two stickers and a set of three stickers on a page, find the set of three stickers when asked for three.
I can when given a domino with one dot and a domino with three dots, locate the domino with one dot when asked for one.
I can when given sets of one to three objects, indicate the set with three objects when asked for three. If the student counts, the teacher asks again for three and reinforce, “This is three.”
I can Teacher holds up 1-3 fingers and asks how many. If student counts, teacher asks again for final number and reinforce, “This is three.”

EE Emerging:
I can repeat the number of objects in sets of 1-3 objects.
I can watch as the teacher uses one scarf, saying, “I have one scarf. How many?”
I can attend to a finger-play of “Three Little Monkeys” told with finger- puppets and repeats how many monkeys.
I can repeat when teacher says how many eyes, nose, ears, mouth, etc. he/she has.
I can point to or indicate items of clothing as teacher counts how many (e.g., “I have two shoes. How many shoes?” “I have one hat. How many hats?” “I have two mittens. How many mittens?” “I have one coat. How many coats?”).

essentialElements.domainName: Number and Operations in Base Ten
essentialElements.text: Decompose quantities less than or equal to five in more than one way.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Compare, compose, and decompose numbers and sets.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.NBT.6 Decompose quantities less than or equal to five in more than one way.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can decompose numbers less than or equal to five in more than one way.
I can when given five books, divide them into two groups in more than one way. I can when given five matchbox cars and two cardboard “garages,” “park” the cars in the garages in varying ways. (First time, student may put two cars in one garage and three cars in the other garage, and teacher asks, “Can you do it a different way this time?” and student continues to distribute the cars in varying ways.)
I can when given five counting blocks, divide them into two groups in more than one way.
I can use teacher-made dice to roll combinations totaling up to five.
I can play a finger game where two students put up random number of fingers on one hand each to create five. If they do, the students’ team earns a point.
I can use a dry erase board to decompose numbers less than five in more than one way.

EE Approaching:
I can decompose numbers less than or equal to five in one way. I can when given a handful of blocks (up to five), separate into two piles in any order. Count and label each pile with teacher assistance. I can Sort up to five items into two groups.
I can when given a group of five tokens composed of two different colors, count out total, sort with teacher by color and count each group.

EE Emerging:
I can identify two sets of the same object (less than five) as they are being decomposed.
I can ask to find the same item as shown somewhere else in the room, bring two of the same items together to make a bigger set.
I can repeat as the teacher decomposes two objects into two groups (e.g., Teacher has two balls, rolls one to the students. Teacher says, “You have one ball, I have one ball. How many balls do you have?” Student rolls it back at prompt. Teacher says, "Now, I have two balls. “ How many balls do I have?” Repeat with various combinations.).
I can repeat as the teacher decomposes two counting bears on the table in a pile (e.g., Teacher says, “Here are two bears. How many bears are there? Take one. Now there is one bear on the table. How many bears are on the table now?”).
I can repeat as the teacher decomposes two books (e.g., Teacher counts aloud the number of books as they are handed to each student. Teacher says, “There are two books. How many books are there? Here is one for you. How many books do you have? Here is one for you. How many books do you have?”).

essentialElements.text: Compare lengths to identify which is longer/shorter or taller/shorter.
essentialElements.conceptualArea: Understand and use measurement principles and units of measure.

workbook.standard: M.EE.1.MD.1 Compare lengths to identify which is longer/shorter or taller/shorter.
workbook.levelDescriptor:
EE At Target :
I can measure the length of objects using non-standard units. I can Measure the length of a given distance using a given non-standard measuring device.
I can count the tiles on the floor to see how many it is from the door of the classroom to the drinking fountain.

EE Approaching:
I can begin to measure from an end point using a non-standard tool. I can Place the measurement tool (paperclip, block), on the left edge.
I can when given an “All About Me” story and body outline, indicate that he or she needs to start at the feet or head and measure to the other end to measure height.
I can when given three pictures with an X at the lower left, upper right, and middle, indicate that the picture with the X at the lower left illustrates the correct place to start measuring.
I can lay nine cubes end-to-end next to a book to see how long the book is.

essentialElements.text: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged within equal groups up to a total of 10.
